_comment: Aaron's own 2001 MX-5 (NB2), from his photos: lowered about 35 mm on coilovers (small arch gap), 15x8 wheels, 205/50R15 200-treadwear tyres. Built from nb2001.json (the stock car, kept for the published-test calibration): body lowered 35 mm (the suspension mounts 35 mm higher in the body at the same static length, so body and centre of mass sit 35 mm lower over the road), coilover springs 7 / 5 kg/mm (392 / 280 lb/in, a common NB street coilover pairing; estimate), the TMeasy tyre stiffer and grippier for a 200TW tyre (estimates: skidpad target 0.98 g, 70-0 160 ft, typical for a lowered NB on 200TW tyres; replace with a measurement of this car when there is one). Stock text follows: 2001-05 Mazda MX-5 Miata (NB2 facelift), US LS five-speed: the car the downloaded Sketchfab model shows (niev, CC BY 4.0). Built from nb1999.json (kept as the calibrated 1999 reference): the BP-Z3 engine with sequential valve timing, 2001 curb weight; chassis, tyres, brakes and gearing carried over from the 1999 Sport.
name: 2001 Roadster (Aaron's)

sources.brake_proportioning: The non-ABS NA/NB Miata has a rear brake proportioning valve; knee at 22 % pedal (about 0.36 g) and 0.25 slope above it make the fronts lock first in a hard stop and in the ISO 7975 brake-in-turn bench (0.5 g circle, pedal 0.3-1.0): at 45 % / 0.35 the car spun at mid pedal (the dynamic front load share at 0.95 g is about 0.70, the brake torque split 0.64). Full-pedal capacity 1600 N m front, 900 rear per wheel: a panic stop reaches about 80 bar line pressure (estimate), and the full pedal must be able to lock the fronts, as on the non-ABS car; the old 1150/650 could not reach the grip of 1.0 g tyres once the valve cut the rear.
sources.engine_friction: Motoring friction 12 N m + 0.005 N m/rpm (27 N m at 3000 rpm, 42 at 6000): a 1.8 L four's friction mean effective pressure of about 1.9 bar at 3000 rpm (estimate from typical SI-engine FMEP), which sets the engine braking on a lift. Full-throttle torque is the published curve either way.
sources.engine_pumping: Closed-throttle pumping 8 N m + 0.001 N m/rpm (11 N m at 3000 rpm): manifold near 0.3 bar absolute on a lift gives a pumping mean effective pressure of about 0.7 bar, x 1.84 L / 4 pi = 10 N m (Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals, ch. 13). With friction that is 38 N m of engine braking at 3000 rpm.
sources.calibration: 0-60 mph 7.8 s (Consumer Guide's 1999-05 Miata test; other listings give up to 8.2 s). No 70-0 or skidpad figure found: the 1999 Car and Driver numbers are carried over as estimates.
sources.springs_bars: Fat Cat Motorsports NB Ride Harmonizer, NB Sport row.
sources.rear_damper: Fat Cat Motorsports Bilstein Hard S rear dyno trace (NB1999Sport.gd).
sources.tyre_tmeasy: TMeasy (G. Rill) with the curve shape of Project Chrono's GuessPassCar70Par set (BSD-3): stiffness 18.4 / 16.0 per unit slip times load, peak slip 0.139 / 0.149, at the nominal load 2557 N and twice it. Grip levels: braking peak 1.10 and sliding 0.91 (0.83 of peak), fitted to the published full-pedal 70-0 stop of 173 ft: at full pedal the front brakes lock these tyres, so the stop is set mostly by the sliding grip (1.20 / 0.963 gave 158.8 ft, 1.10 / 0.85 gave 184.7 ft); lateral peak 1.064 = 0.963 x 1.105, the calibrated skidpad grip, sliding at Chrono's 0.833 of it.
sources.tyre_slip: Slip-ratio curve flat (slip_ratio_falloff 0, CarSpec default): the only braking figure, the 173 ft full-pedal stop without ABS, pins the grip of a locked tyre at 0.963, and a fall-off would need a peak above it with no measurement behind it (peak 1.07 sliding to 0.963 raised trail-braking grip 5.3 % in checks/CombinedSlip.gd). Peak grip 0.963 and lateral scale 1.105 as calibrated before the curve.
sources.estimates: Front damping, tyre curve, camber gain, inertia and differential bias are development estimates (see Powertrain.gd and NB1999Sport.gd comments).
sources.engine: Mazda US specification for the 2001 MX-5 Miata: 1.8 L BP-Z3 with sequential valve timing, 142 hp at 7000 rpm, 125 lb-ft at 5500 rpm; curve shape from the 1999 BP-4W scaled to those points.
sources.mass: Curb weight 2,387 lb (LS, cars.com and autotk.com specification listings); inertia scaled from the 1999 car by mass.
sources.body: The NB2 body has added bracing and is stiffer than the NB1; the simulation has no chassis compliance yet, so it changes nothing here.

calibration_open: 70-0 and skidpad: no published NB2 brake or skidpad test was found, so the 1999 Sport's 173 ft and 0.89 g stand in (same brakes and tyres here). The 0-60 target, 7.8 s, is the one published NB2 figure found and is held (7.75 s on the bench, untuned).

card.handling: Light, quick steering (2.6 turns lock to lock with power assist) and mild tuck-in on lifting in a corner; reviewers call it balanced and forgiving.
card.sources: Turning circle 9.2 m (30.2 ft): cars-data.com NB 1.8 specification. Curb 2,387 lb: the car file's NB2 LS listing. Steering 15:1, 2.6 turns: GoAuto 2001 MX-5 review. Handling: Cars.com 1999 review, Grassroots Motorsports owners.
